next_experiment: One consenting pair of utilities supplies eight redacted nominal requirement cards and inventory constraints; one manufacturer supplies a current batch quotation and capacity commitment. Two engineers independently map and check every original requirement, compare a conventional broker using the same inputs, and accept only a signed site-specific conformity disposition. Obtain explicit rights and financing terms before any paid action.
prior_approach: DOE taxonomy/configuration/interchangeability matrices; National Grid engineering-led SKU reduction; pooled distributor procurement; exact finite planning
remaining_gap: Can several actual utilities and one supplier agree to a shared batch without losing site-specific requirements or stranding legacy inventory?

scale.basis: Explicit threshold scenario, entirely unverified commercial/production assumptions. Net benefit per unit is after buyer fees, implementation, financing and the competent alternative. Not a market-size or revenue estimate; no probability times speculative upside.

sources.does_not_establish: An authorized buyer brief, exact eligible inputs, valid engineering mapping, supplier/lab quote, current permissions or our performance
sources.supports: Published problem context and established prior approaches, not our proposed recipe truth

stopping_condition: Stop before manufacturing if any indispensable requirement cannot be translated losslessly, acceptance is unresolved, the supplier cannot honor capacity, or complete buyer/provider economics fail against the broker.
what_prior_approach_already_delivers: The transcript describes implemented engineering-led consolidation and supplier collaboration. These are serious available conventional methods, not a hypothetical weak baseline
why_now: DOE published configuration and interchangeability resources and concrete SKU reduction work in March 2026; frontier tools can assist extraction, but do not verify engineering truth
